answer: Enrollment binds a name to one identity kernel and a delayed escrow, not a free key. The kernel commits a TEE quote, one payout address, and a merklized log of the last 128 work receipts. The agent locks 12,000 units of jade that unlock only after a four-epoch gale of unannounced probes, each demanding a same-TEE signature over a random log leaf. If a second name reuses the quote or payout address, both escrows are burned and two-thirds of the jade goes to the first auditor with a colliding proof. An honest operator funds one kernel; a farm's slash risk rises with every clone.
